$comment: THE CONVENTION LEDGER.  Read `check.py --only conventions` for the guard that
enforces it, and the `purpose` block below for why it exists.
ANCHORING.  Every key in `declarations` is `<module path>::<declaration name>`.
There are no line numbers anywhere in this file, and there must never be:
a ledger pinned to offsets fails on edits that have nothing to do with it,
which is how `extract/test_parser.py` came to be red.
DRIFT.  This is a committed snapshot of a corpus that changes daily, so it
goes stale by construction.  The guard makes staleness LOUD rather than
silent: an entry naming a declaration that no longer exists FAILS, and a
declaration matching a `complete` quantity with no entry FAILS.  Renaming or
moving a ledgered definition is therefore a two-file edit on purpose.
purpose: A convention is not visible to Lean.  Nei's G_ST, Hudson's F_ST and the
per-branch drift F are all reals in [0,1), all named `fst`, and all three
type-check in each other's place.  This corpus has been burned by exactly
that: the factor-of-4 F_ST error, a Nei body under the name `hudsonFst`,
and a within-population heterozygosity loss documented as a
between-population variance ratio.  Each was found by a person reading
against a paper.  This file is that reading, written down as data, so the
next occurrence is caught by a script instead.

hudson.means: Hudson's F_ST: the ratio of averages whose denominator is the BETWEEN-subgroup heterozygosity p1(1-p2)+p2(1-p1), equivalently 1 - E[T_within]/E[T_between] on coalescence times.
hudson.source: Hudson, Slatkin & Maddison (1992); Bhatia, Patterson, Sankararaman & Price (2013), Genome Research 23:1514-1521.

nei-gst.means: Nei's G_ST: one minus mean within-subgroup heterozygosity over TOTAL-pool heterozygosity 2*pbar*(1-pbar).  Exactly G = H/(2-H) of the Hudson value, hence about HALF of it at small differentiation and equal only at 0 and 1.

identity-probability.means: F as the probability that two gene copies drawn from ONE deme are identical by descent, the 1/(1 + 4*Ne*rate) family.  Derived once for an abstract rate by `ibdFlowStep_fixedPoint`, so mutation and migration share it.
identity-probability.source: Malecot's (4Nu+1)^-1, standardly cited to Kimura & Crow (1964), Genetics 49:725-738; Wright (1931) for the migration case.
identity-probability.compatible_with_hudson: Deliberately NOT declared incompatible with `hudson`.  In the island model at low mutation the equilibrium identity probability IS the Hudson F_ST; that identification is what `ibdFlowStep_fixedPoint` and `fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium_isFixedPoint` state.  See `open_questions` below for what is nevertheless missing.

per-branch-drift.means: The single-lineage Wright F measured against the ANCESTOR: the fraction of ancestral heterozygosity one lineage has lost, 1 - H_t/H_0, approaching 1 - exp(-tau).  NOT a between-population quantity.

inherited.means: The body transforms an F supplied by the caller and asserts no estimator of its own.  Whatever convention the caller used, this body returns.  Never incompatible with anything, because it commits to nothing.

narrow-sense.means: h2 = V_A / V_P with V_P = V_A + V_D + V_I + V_E.  The denominator INCLUDES the non-additive components; V_A/(V_A+V_E) is a different and larger number.
narrow-sense.source: Falconer & Mackay, Introduction to Quantitative Genetics, 4th ed.

snp.means: h2_SNP = tagged additive variance / V_P.  Bounded above by narrow-sense, and the gap is the untagged additive variance.

liability-scale.means: Heritability on the unobserved liability scale of a binary trait, converted from the observed scale by the prevalence and the threshold height.
liability-scale.source: Dempster & Lerner (1950); Lee, Wray, Goddard & Visscher (2011), AJHG 88:294-305.

am-inflated.means: Heritability as OBSERVED in an assortatively mating population, inflated over the random-mating value by the equilibrium variance factor.  An axis orthogonal to narrow/SNP/liability.

derived-share.means: A ratio, share, enrichment or fraction BUILT FROM heritabilities rather than a heritability.  Its own value is not a heritability and must not be read as one.

bridges.says: Hudson = 2G/(1+G) everywhere, so the discrepancy is 2x as G -> 0 and cannot be absorbed by any recalibration constant.
tau/(1+tau) < 1 - exp(-tau) at every positive tau: the pairwise estimator and the per-branch drift F are different numbers, 0.500 against 0.632 at tau = 1.

fst.why: The corpus's most expensive recurring bug class.  Nei's G_ST between two demes is half the per-branch drift F and a quarter of the pairwise F_ST written as a variance ratio; three separate repairs have been needed.

h2.why: A docstring on `additive_pgs_ceiling` labelled V_A/(V_A+V_E) as narrow-sense heritability, which is larger than the real one by V_P/(V_A+V_E).  No incompatible PAIR is declared yet: the h2 conventions are ordered by inequalities the corpus proves rather than being rival estimators of one number, so the connectivity rule is inactive here and only completeness and constants apply.

r2.why: REGISTERED BUT NOT YET LEDGERED.  44 declarations carry it and the r / r-squared / D' distinction is a known hazard (`tagR2` divides by GENOTYPIC 2p(1-p), and reading the variances as allelic p(1-p) scales the result by four).  `scope: unscoped` means the guard checks nothing here; it is recorded so the next pass has a place to put the work, not so it looks covered.

alpha.why: REGISTERED BUT NOT YET LEDGERED.  sd-ratio versus variance-ratio alpha is on the fleet's hazard list; no corpus declaration currently carries `alpha` as a camel-case word, so there is nothing to ledger today and the entry exists to catch the first one.

open_questions: There is no theorem anywhere in the corpus relating the `identity-probability` family (1/(1+4*Ne*rate)) to the `hudson` family (tau/(1+tau)).  They are believed to agree in the island model at low mutation, which is why they are not declared incompatible, but the belief is not machine-checked.  A bridge theorem would let `identity-probability` join the incompatibility graph and tighten this guard.

`PortabilityDrift.pairwiseFstFromBranches` is ledgered `hudson` on its OUTPUT while its two ARGUMENTS are per-branch drift values.  The ledger has one convention slot per declaration and cannot express that; the mixed reading is recorded in the entry's `note`.

$comment: Constants and exponents READ AGAINST THE PUBLISHED SOURCE and frozen here, so a
later edit turning a 4 into a 2 fails mechanically instead of waiting for
somebody to re-read the paper.  These carry no `quantity` and no `convention`:
they are outside the fst/h2 families and only the staleness and constants rules
A mismatch here does NOT mean the body is wrong.  It means the body and this
record disagree, and the way to settle that is to re-read the cited source --
which is the entire point of writing the value down.

Calibrator/LDDecayTheory.lean::ohtaKimur.source: Ohta & Kimura (1971): sigma_d^2 = (10 + rho)/((2 + rho)(11 + rho)), rho = 4*Ne*c.  Value 5/11 at rho = 0.

Calibrator/DGP.lean::scaledMigrationRate.source: M = 4*Ne*m, the same scaling applied to gene flow.

Calibrator/CovarianceStructure.lean::lds.source: Bulik-Sullivan et al. (2015), Nature Genetics 47:291-295: E[chi2] = N*h2*l/M + N*a + 1.  The 1 is the null expectation of a 1-df statistic and is what makes the LDSC intercept a confounding diagnostic; the confounding term is NOT divided by M.

Calibrator/TransferLearningPGS.lean::pin.source: sqrt(2*KL), the L1-convention Pinsker bound.  Deliberately NOT the tight sqrt(KL/2): the definition's own docstring records that it is loose by exactly a factor of two, measured over 200000 distribution pairs.

Calibrator/TransferLearningPGS.lean::gau.source: exp(-2*I) is the Gaussian residual-variance fraction; the 2 is fixed by half a nat costing exactly one e-fold.

Calibrator/LDDecayTheory.lean::admixture.source: Chakraborty & Weiss (1988) hybrid-isolation model: D = alpha*(1-alpha)*dp1*dp2.  The weight is the VARIANCE alpha(1-alpha), not alpha; simulation excludes the linear form at 1627 sems.

Calibrator/LDDecayTheory.lean::driftLDRe.source: (1-c)^2 * (1 - 1/(2*Ne)).  The exponent 2 on (1-c) is the two lineage pairs; the 2*Ne is the diploid coalescent scale.

Calibrator/LDDecayTheory.lean::ldRetenti.source: The elementary two-locus recursion (1-r)*(1 - 1/(2*Ne)).  NOT Ohta-Kimura, which is the sigma_d^2 form above.

Calibrator/EpistasisAndNonAdditivity.lea.source: Falconer & Mackay: alpha = a + d*(1 - 2p).  The dominance term vanishes at p = 1/2 and reverses across it.
V_AA = beta12^2 * 2p1q1 * 2p2q2 under HWE and linkage equilibrium; the two 2s are genotypic variances, not allelic.

Calibrator/PowerAnalysis.lean::noncentra.source: NCP = n*beta^2*2p(1-p): beta enters quadratically and p through the GENOTYPE variance 2p(1-p), not the allelic p(1-p).

Calibrator/PopulationGeneticsFoundations.source: Malecot / Kimura-Weiss (1964) 1-D decay scale L = sqrt(m*sigma^2/(2*mu)); the mutation rate is mandatory and the deme size does not enter.

Calibrator/PCCorrectability/Threshold.le.source: 4*F*effectiveSubgroupSize.  The 4 is recovered as 3.9920 +- 0.0045 by inverting the BBP eigenvalue law on simulated genotypes with F measured as genuine Hudson F_ST.

Calibrator/PortabilityDrift.lean::hetMut.source: theta/(1+theta) with theta = 4*Ne*mu: the infinite-alleles equilibrium heterozygosity, complement of Malecot's identity probability.

Calibrator/PortabilityDrift.lean::coales.source: tau = t/(2*Ne).  This is the 2*Ne that is NOT the 4*Ne of a scaled rate; it is a TIME scale, the mean pairwise coalescence time.

Calibrator/AssortativeMatingPGS.lean::am.source: Fisher (1918) linearisation: mid-parent variance (1/2)V(1 + r*h2) plus segregation (1/2)V0.  The segregation term uses the RANDOM-MATING V0; using V collapses the recursion to one whose only fixed point is 0.
V_A/(1 - r*h2), the fixed point of amVarianceStep, with h2 held at its random-mating value.

Calibrator/Conventions.lean::hudsonFst.source: Bhatia, Patterson, Sankararaman & Price (2013), Genome Research 23:1514-1521.

Calibrator/PopulationGeneticsFoundations.note: The heterozygosity form (H_T - H_S)/H_T; same statistic as `neiGst`, different arguments.
The 4 is the total-pool denominator 4*pbar*(1-pbar).  Changing it to 2 turns this into a different statistic that still type-checks.
t/(t + 2*Ne) is tau/(1+tau) with tau = t/(2*Ne); the 2 is the ploidy in the coalescent time scale.
1 - H/H0 with H0 the ANCESTRAL heterozygosity.  Its own docstring measures it against the classical (1 - 1/(2Ne))^t decay, which is the per-branch reading and not an estimator.
The deme correction enters LINEARLY here.  Crow & Aoki (1984) square it, but that is the correction for Nei's G_ST, a different statistic.
Two independent 4s: 4*Ne*m and 4*Ne*mu.  Either one dropping to 2 halves the corresponding scaled rate.

Calibrator/DGP.lean::fstMutationDriftEqu.note: NOT the Wright island-model result despite the shared shape; that one is in the migration rate.

Calibrator/DGP.lean::fstDriftFlowStep.note: The leading 2 on (mig + mu) is the two lineages that can independently escape the identity class.  A 1 there halves both homogenising forces.

Calibrator/PortabilityDrift.lean::fstFro.note: tau/(1+tau).  The saturation law; `fstFromTau_lt_coalescenceCdf` is what keeps it distinct from 1 - exp(-tau).

Calibrator/PortabilityDrift.lean::pairwi.note: The 2 is the MEAN of the branch taus.  A sum instead of a mean double-counts the split time and was measured 50 percent high at up to 59 sems.
Output is pairwise; the two ARGUMENTS are per-branch drift values.  Recorded in open_questions: the ledger has one slot per declaration and cannot carry both.

Calibrator/PortabilityDrift.lean::steppi.note: Takes `fst_neighbor` and returns a distance-`d` value in whatever convention that was.

Calibrator/PortabilityDrift.lean::fstMig.note: The infinite-island LIMIT.  `islandFstFiniteDemes` carries the finite-deme correction.
The linearised step: (1-m)^2 approximated as 1-2m, so the 2 on m is the linearisation and not a ploidy.

Calibrator/PortabilityDrift.lean::Mutati.note: Within-population identity probability despite the `fst` in the name.

Calibrator/DemographicHistory.lean::demo.note: Built on `coalFst`, hence Hudson.  The 4 is the scaled migration rate 4*Ne*m; the superseded quadratic sibling squares both m and sigma.

Calibrator/DemographicHistory.lean::step.note: A superseded candidate kept as a discriminand: quadratic in m and in sigma where the surviving form is linear.

Calibrator/DemographicHistory.lean::admi.note: (1-alpha)^2 scaling of a supplied fst_AB.  The exponent 2 is the admixture weight and a 1 there is a different model.

Calibrator/AssortativeMatingPGS.lean::ib.note: Isolation by distance; its own docstring pins `N` as a DENSITY rather than a deme size by dimensional analysis.

Calibrator/SerialFounderChain.lean::seri.note: tau/(T_within + tau), the coalescence-time ratio for the chain.

Calibrator/VarianceComponents.lean::narr.note: V_A/(V_A+V_D+V_I+V_E).  V_A/(V_A+V_E) is NOT this quantity and is larger whenever V_D+V_I > 0.

Calibrator/VarianceComponents.lean::liab.source: Dempster & Lerner (1950); Lee et al. (2011), AJHG 88:294-305.
Calibrator/VarianceComponents.lean::liab.note: The exponent 2 is the squared threshold height z^2.  A 1 there is a different scale conversion entirely.

Calibrator/TransferLearningPGS.lean::sha.note: Additive variance computed through a shared LD kernel, still divided by the phenotypic variance.

Calibrator/AncestrySpecificArchitecture..note: h2_true * mean tagging r-squared is the tagged share, which is what h2_SNP measures.

Calibrator/PowerAnalysis.lean::heritabil.note: n/(n+C) is the FRACTION of heritability recovered at sample size n, not a heritability.

Calibrator/SelectionArchitecture.lean::e.note: Total heritability divided by the locus count: a per-locus share.
